verdict.root_cause: The failing component is cart, not checkout. Every complete trace shows checkout's full fan-out — cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping/quote, payment, email, flagd — finishing in single-digit milliseconds with no checkout span flagged ERROR [tr_b25e9b250796]. The only explicit attribution on the board is in frontend's logs: a checkout call returning gRPC INTERNAL that wraps a cart lookup failure whose name resolver produced zero addresses, plus repeated gRPC UNAVAILABLE with transport-level host-unreachable to a backend at 172.18.0.24:7070, last error stamped 22:49:58 [tr_213f84c62d86]. Two independent call paths — frontend's own client and checkout's cart client — fail simultaneously with connection-establishment failures rather than timeouts, which is the signature of the cart endpoint dropping off the network and service-discovery plane. Checkout's error ratio steps off an exactly-zero floor at 22:47:31 and spikes to ~67% while most buckets stay near zero [tr_acd19f2db44a, tr_85cfd0120a9a], matching only the subset of requests needing a cart round-trip failing. Checkout's own change history is empty [tr_5ec324b65a06, tr_045921c00b65].
verdict.reasoning: Checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator alerted together because they are the call chain above cart; errors propagate toward the caller. The failing trace stops at frontend/POST [tr_b25e9b250796], ruling out a checkout-internal throw but not naming the callee — the frontend logs supply that, with a cart failure surfaced through checkout and direct EHOSTUNREACH to one backend address [tr_213f84c62d86]. The mode is connection establishment, not waiting, so dependency_latency is excluded; a frozen process would still accept and hang callers rather than return host-unreachable. Partial error ratios with zero minimums [tr_85cfd0120a9a] fit an intermittently unreachable dependency, not a total outage. Checkout emitting zero log lines [tr_2fb471319f1f] while actively producing spans is a telemetry gap, not silence of the process. The fix is restoring cart's reachability and endpoint registration.
open_questions: No dispatch examined cart at all — its logs, metrics, process state and change history are unexamined; cart is named by inference from two callers' error text.
172.18.0.24:7070 is never resolved to a service name; it is assumed to be cart, and could instead be a second affected backend.
Whether cart is running-but-isolated or simply gone (crashed, scaled to zero, failed rollout) is unsettled — 'zero addresses' fits both, and this is the main risk to the fault class.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart's process or pod terminated entirely, so service discovery deregistered it and callers see zero addresses and unreachable hosts.
alternatives.why_not: Indistinguishable from a partition using only caller-side evidence, but cart's own absence from discovery plus host-unreachable is more commonly an isolation symptom; no cart-side signal was collected to confirm process death.

alternatives.root_cause: A service-discovery or DNS layer change broke resolution of the cart endpoint, leaving the cart service itself healthy.
alternatives.why_not: No change record was ever queried outside checkout at radius 0, and the EHOSTUNREACH on a concrete IP:port indicates connectivity failure beyond mere name resolution.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any series is expected. What should happen next is a diagnostic dispatch against cart itself — its logs, its process/container state, and its change history — plus a resolution of 172.18.0.24:7070 to a service name. That would either confirm cart is running-but-isolated (favoring a network reattach) or show it is gone/crashed (favoring restart or rollback). Until then the observable state stays as it is: frontend continuing to log gRPC UNAVAILABLE host-unreachable to 172.18.0.24:7070 and checkout's error ratio continuing to spike off its zero floor.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if cart is in fact simply crashed and a restart_service on cart would have cleared it — in which case the cost of waiting is the elapsed minutes of ~67% error spikes on cart-dependent checkout requests. It is also wrong if a dispatch on cart turns up a deploy or config change inside the window, which would have made rollback_image or revert_config the correct and immediately available action. Either observation falsifies this abstention and should be acted on at once.
proposal.risk: The named fix class for this verdict is 'reconnect', and reconnect_service is explicitly unavailable in this executor. Substituting restart_service for it would be acting past the evidence: restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and no dispatch examined cart's process state at all — cart is named only by inference from two callers' error text, and 172.18.0.24:7070 is never resolved to a service name. If that address is a second affected backend rather than cart, recreating cart's container destroys its in-process cache, drops every live cart connection, and leaves the actual partition in place while making the telemetry harder to read. rollback_image and revert_config are equally unsupported: the only change history on the board is checkout's, and it is empty [tr_5ec324b65a06]; no prior image tag or configuration for cart is recorded here, so both preconditions fail outright.
proposal.blast_radius: Nothing changes, so no one sees anything new. The cost is borne by whoever is already affected: checkout's cart-dependent PlaceOrder path keeps failing at up to ~67% in its worst buckets, frontend keeps surfacing those as gRPC INTERNAL to frontend-proxy and load-generator, and the four alerted seeds (checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator) stay alerting. Cart's other callers reached from frontend remain exposed to the same unresolvable endpoint.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical, simultaneous alerts across checkout, frontend and the proxy with load-generator following a minute later indicate a real user-facing failure, not a quiet world. No open incidents to attribute it to and the alert pattern alone doesn't single out a cause among checkout's or frontend's dependencies.
